request.spec:
The order of the due steps changes: the late charge is now worked out on the rate figure alone,
or on the figure a statement bound, and the floor is applied last: a claim's live due is the
greater of the floor in force on its date and its figure plus its late charge. A statement now
binds the rate figure, not the floored one. Settled figures stay frozen; a correction is unchanged
(no floor, no charge).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The order of the due steps changes: the late charge is now worked out on the rate figure alone,
or on the figure a statement bound, and the floor is applied last: a claim's live due is the
greater of the floor in force on its date and its figure plus its late charge. A statement now
binds the rate figure, not the floored one. Settled figures stay frozen; a correction is unchanged
(no floor, no charge).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The floor is now applied last. A claim's live due is the greater of the floor in force on its date and its figure plus its late charge. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The same calculation lives in two places, and I changed both:

- **Server, `statement/Dues.java`:** working out a claim's figure no longer applies the floor. That figure is the settled due, else the statement-bound figure, else the rate figure. The floor is applied once at the end, when the due shown on the row is computed. That one function feeds the row values, rollups, period closes, settling and the status log, so they all follow the new order. Corrections still get no floor and no charge, and settled dues are returned unchanged.
- **Statements, `statement/SaveStatement.java`:** taking a statement now stores the rate figure without the floor, so the floor and late charge keep following the sheet afterwards.
- **Front end, `features/rates/rates.ts`:** the screen's own due calculation (`claimDue`) now matches the server's: figure plus late charge, then the floor.

I also updated the doc comments in `SaveClaimStatus.java` and `ClaimStatusChange.java` to describe the new order.

I didn't change any stored data. Statements taken before this change still hold their old figure with the floor already in it. The bare rate figure wasn't stored, so it can't be recovered. Those claims will show the right answer whenever the floor is at or above their old figure, but the late charge on them will still be worked out on the floored figure until the person gets a new statement.
